data.name: Glorch's Great Escape: Walking is for Chumps
data.detailed_description:
What is this game?

Glorch's Great Escape is a challenging puzzle platformer where your only weapon is the almighty "Telenade," a grenade with a built-in teleporter. Guide Glorch from his prison cell through the defenses of his captor's space station, and help him escape on his impounded ship.


You'll be solving plenty of difficult platforming puzzles and scenarios, finding some secrets, smashing a few robots, and generally dying a whole bunch of times. We've made sure to include a freshly composed jazzy soundtrack to help keep your platformer rage levels in check.

So what is a Telenade, and why is Walking for Chumps?

Glorch can waddle left and right if he must, but he isn't even going to attempt to jump. That sounds like too much effort. Besides, why bother walking when you can just teleport wherever you want to go within range of a short throw? Only chumps would do that.

What is a Glorch anyway?

Glorch is a member of the Glorches, a race of...ahem..."big boned" purple aliens. They are the inventors of the Telenade.

How about a feature rundown?

  • Based on our top 20 Ludum Dare 32 entry of the same name
  • 24 challenging levels, with additional extra-difficult "challenge" levels to unlock by reaching par milestones
  • Plenty of varied puzzles and scenarios to figure out, dangers to avoid, secrets to find, and deadly pits to fall into
  • Each level has been lovingly hand-crafted to find just the right balance of difficult and satisfying
  • Jazzy soundtrack? Yeah.

reviews.review:
[quote][url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/32732116-IndieGems/]Follow our curator page: [b]IndieGems[/b] if you like and want to see more reviews like this one.[/url][/quote]

[i]Glorch's Great Escape: Walking is for Chumps[/i] claims to be a difficult puzzle platformer, and it sure is exactly that. The difficulty level is not casual and very unforgiving, but the game does exactly what it's advertised to do. Currently the game is on sale at 65% off at 1.04 USD (Base 2.99), I think the discount price is probably what I would think is ideal for this game. I say this in all honesty, this is one of those games that will cause the player some sheer frustration due to its difficulty, but not due to glitches or other issues.

The gameplay is simple, you move left and right with A and D, and you aim and click your left mouse button to throw your "telenade." Where this ends up is where you will ultimately teleport to, and you can cut this short by clicking your mouse button again. There is no jumping, and there's very little walking. All of your actions are by teleportation. I think the subtitle should read "Walking and Jumping Are For Chumps," but hey, the actual name works well too.

The actions are simple, but the platforming is so very difficult. You have to make split second decisions on what to do and how to react next, otherwise you are easily caught in an endless loop of redoing the same thing again and again. This is a bit frustrating, and a bit addictive as well. 

I just watched the game trailer after playing quite a while without making too much progress. The game is only 24 levels with a few unlockable extra-difficult challenge levels. I don't think I will ever see these levels myself, to be honest. The base levels are hard enough for me. Fortunately any level you have completed is now unlocked and you can redo only that one as you wish. This is important because there is an achievement for getting 3 stars on each level. I must say, no level is easy to achieve all 3 stars, except for maybe the very first level.

The difficulty of the game comes in multiple layers, the constant gravitation effect on the main character, the fact that there are quite a few death-fail states possible, mobile enemy projectiles that are predictable but really difficult to avoid, plus the simple puzzle element of having certain spaces where your character can pass through, but your telenade cannot, and also vice versa. Put them all together, you got yourself in a really tough situation. (There are some secrets to find too, for me it was difficult enough trying to complete the basic levels that I have seen.

[h1]Controls[/h1]
As above, keyboard A/D and mouse for aim and throwing/detonating your telenade. 

[h1]Graphics and Music[/h1]
Graphics are 2D platforming with a simple yet pleasant retro style. 

The music tracks are decent, nothing too fancy, but not bad either.

[h1]Audience[/h1]
Not for the casual player, not for the easily enraged player. This is really really difficult. And the mechanics may put off some players. Definitely look at the trailer and decide whether or not you even want to take this dive.

[h1]Price[/h1]
As mentioned, base price of 2.99 USD and currently on sale at 65% off at 1.04 USD. I think the sale price is rather appropriate.

[h1]Positives[/h1]
+No bugs in playing for almost an hour
+Simple to learn, so easy to pick up
+Interesting idea, to take the player away from the traditional puzzle platforming a bit
+Reasonably priced

[h1]Negatives[/h1]
-Challenging, perhaps a bit too challenging
-Some may find the overall game to be too simplistic in gameplay. It has a casual look and feel but extremely difficult  to actually play
-In maps when you cannot see the whole field for that level, it would be nice to have some way to actually see whole level to make your plans--I do not think you can at this time

[h1]Conclusion[/h1]
[i]Glorch's Great Escape: Walking is for Chumps[/i] is challenging and perhaps too difficult, but it's an interesting indie title that may also give you a challenge for your skills and your split-second decision making. Currently it's on sale and I would say it's worth the sale price. As for your time and your style, you have to decide for yourself--go look at the trailer. You will probably experience many failures on many levels before finding your way out. The puzzle aspect is there constantly and there is little left to chance, given the level designs. There are too many fail states and a lot of timed actions to guarantee that this game is not casual in experience. The important thing to note is that regardless of actual difficulty, there's not much in the way of bugs that cause additional frustration--of course there was enough of that anyway.
